title: Product runs whose team snapshot exists but whose independent audit persisted NO verdict
why_this_file_exists: Between runs 39025961835 and 39042713389 the product lane produced SIX consecutive team snapshots with no persisted audit verdict. The prior cycle's product/audit_pack.py docstring cited 'raw GitHub check-run annotations saved under results/product/orchestration/' for these failures; that directory was never committed, so the citations were not auditable from the tree. This file replaces them with evidence a third party can re-derive from the repository and the remote in one command, and it labels every claim by what it actually rests on. Run 39047235085 added the sixth entry and wired this registry into product/audit_pack.py check non_verdicted_runs_registry, which re-derives the whole classification from local refs/remotes/origin/cycle/core/product/* and fails on any drift.
how_to_reproduce: for r in 39042713389 39039195228 39034350468 39031213637 39027045675 39025961835; do printf '%s team=%s audit=%s\n' "$r" "$(git ls-remote --heads origin refs/heads/cycle/core/product/$r/team | wc -l)" "$(git ls-remote --heads origin refs/heads/cycle/core/product/$r/audit | wc -l)"; done
git for-each-ref 'refs/remotes/origin/cycle/core/product/*/audit'   # offline equivalent: lists only runs that WERE audited; 39025961835..39042713389 are absent
git ls-files -- results/audit/product/ | grep -E 'CYCLE_(39042713389|39039195228|39034350468|39031213637|39027045675|39025961835)_GATE.json'   # expect no output
python3 product/audit_pack.py --run-id local --no-tests --json | jq '.checks[] | select(.id=="non_verdicted_runs_registry")'   # the same classification, asserted against refs

detection_rule.non_verdicted: refs/heads/cycle/core/product/<run>/audit is ABSENT on origin. The audit job's final step is 'Persist audit snapshot', which pushes that branch. Absence therefore means no gate file was ever persisted, so the run has no verdict of any kind - it is NOT a PASS, NOT a REVISE and NOT a BLOCKED.
detection_rule.verdicted_not_promoted: the audit branch EXISTS but results/audit/product/CYCLE_<run>_GATE.json is absent from the accepted base (lab/product). A verdict was written and not accepted. This is a normal outcome, not an operational failure, and is listed separately so the two classes are never conflated.
detection_rule.accepted: the gate file is on the accepted base. Only 39019268074 is in this class.

structural_reading.not_a_product_verdict: Six non-verdicts in a row is an orchestration signal, not six product rejections. Factory-wide requirement 20 already governs the largest family of causes (provider rotation / overload: an audit or producer job that dies on provider death is NOT a verdict, NOT a product defect and NOT a human-gate problem). No run in this file is evidence against the v52 endgame, and none of it may be cited as if a bar had been missed.
producer_side_mitigations_landed: product/audit_pack.py: one command that recomputes every v52 endgame claim from committed artifacts in under 70 s, so the auditor verifies instead of reconstructing under the 2700s work quantum (the mechanism that is documented, for other runs, in reports/product/CYCLE_39011220761_RESUME.md)

product/audit_pack.py: the auditor's write scope is stated in the pack's own output as the exact two relative paths the workflow permits, because exit 3 'auditor crossed scope' is the one failure mode with a committed annotation (reports/product/CYCLE_38766812030.md); a one-line auditor quickstart (run from /tmp/lex_team with --out /tmp/lex_audit_pack) is printed on every console run since 39047235085

product/audit_pack.py: BLOCKED_MISSING_DEPENDENCY triage, because core-lane.yml installs no Python dependencies in either the team or the audit job, so a bare audit checkout previously reported six environment failures as PRODUCT failures

product/audit_pack.py: bootstrap_dependencies now verifies pip's exit 0 against a FRESH-interpreter import probe (run 39047235085 observed installed:true alongside missing_after:[numpy,scipy,sklearn,pytest] from in-process finder-cache staleness, a contradiction an auditor could misread as a failed install)

claim_ceiling: This file reports workflow-orchestration facts only: which branches exist and which gate files are committed. It asserts no product quality, re-measures no frozen bar, scores no label or geometry criterion, and makes no claim about whether any decision is supporting, contrary or limiting. It does not assert that any of these runs passed or failed an audit - six of them were never audited at all. The registry's consistency with the remote is asserted only by product-owned check non_verdicted_runs_registry, never by this file alone.
